evals.prompt: Our company's Apache web server was compromised last night. We have 3 days of access logs (access.log, ~2.3GB) and error logs from the past week. The server hosts a customer portal with a MySQL backend. Our SOC noticed unusual outbound traffic at 03:47 UTC and the server was isolated at 04:15 UTC. Analyze the web server logs to identify: (1) the initial attack vector and entry point, (2) all IP addresses involved in the attack, (3) the timeline of attacker actions from first probe to data exfiltration, (4) what data was accessed or exfiltrated, and (5) any persistence mechanisms installed. The logs are at /var/log/apache2/ on the preserved disk image mounted at /mnt/evidence. Provide a full investigation report with timeline, root cause, impact assessment, and recommendations.
evals.expected_output: A comprehensive web2 log analysis investigation report containing: (1) Executive summary classifying the incident type (e.g., SQL injection leading to RCE, or webshell upload), (2) A detailed timeline table with timestamps (UTC), source IPs, HTTP methods, URIs, response codes, and user-agents showing the full attack progression from initial reconnaissance through exploitation to exfiltration, (3) Identification of the initial attack vector with specific log evidence (e.g., SQL injection in login form, file upload vulnerability, or credential stuffing), (4) All attacker IP addresses with geolocation and whether they used VPN/Tor/proxies, (5) Evidence of data exfiltration including volume estimates based on response sizes and unusual download patterns, (6) Any persistence mechanisms (webshell uploads, cron job modifications, new user accounts) with corresponding log entries, (7) Root cause analysis explaining the vulnerability that was exploited and why detection took until 03:47 UTC, (8) Impact assessment covering data compromised, systems affected, and duration of access, (9) Specific recommendations for remediation and detection improvements, (10) All findings backed by specific log line references with timestamps and raw log excerpts as evidence.

evals.prompt: A DeFi protocol on Ethereum was exploited 6 hours ago for approximately 3,400 ETH (~$8.2M). The exploit tx hash is 0x7a3f...e91b. The protocol team has frozen withdrawals but funds are still moving. Trace the stolen funds on-chain to determine: (1) the full fund flow from the exploit contract through any intermediary addresses to current resting places, (2) whether funds have been deposited to mixers (Tornado Cash etc.), DEXs, or centralized exchanges, (3) the attacker's funding source — how was the exploit contract originally funded (CEX withdrawal, DEX swap, bridge, or another DeFi protocol), (4) any address clustering that links the attacker to other known exploit addresses or prior incidents, (5) current status of the funds (still moving, dormant in EOA, or deposited to mixer/exchange). Use Etherscan, Dune Analytics, and any other on-chain tools available. Provide a complete fund tracing report with transaction hashes, timestamps, and visual fund flow description.
evals.expected_output: A comprehensive web3 fund tracing investigation report containing: (1) Executive summary with total value stolen, current fund status, and recovery prospects, (2) Complete transaction-by-transaction fund flow from the exploit transaction through all intermediary hops, with tx hashes, block numbers, timestamps (UTC), and ETH amounts at each step, (3) Identification of the exploit mechanism (flash loan, price oracle manipulation, reentrancy, access control bug) based on calldata analysis, (4) Attacker funding source analysis showing how the exploit contract was capitalized, with the original funding tx hash and source (CEX/DEX/bridge/other), (5) Current fund locations with specific addresses and amounts, clearly distinguishing between funds in EOAs, DEX liquidity, mixers, and centralized exchanges, (6) If funds went through Tornado Cash or other mixers, identification of the deposit tx and any withdrawal txs if they exist, (7) Address clustering analysis linking the attacker address to related addresses based on common funding sources, timing patterns, and behavioral fingerprints, (8) Attribution assessment with confidence level (speculative/moderate/high/confirmed) and any known threat actor matches, (9) Recovery recommendations including exchange contact procedures, chainalysis/TRM reporting, and law enforcement referral steps, (10) All transaction hashes and addresses documented for evidence preservation.

evals.prompt: We are the incident response team for a mid-size fintech company. At approximately 14:30 UTC today, our fraud detection system flagged 47 unauthorized wire transfers totaling $2.3M from customer accounts to external bank accounts over a 3-hour window. The transfers were initiated through our internal admin portal. We have: VPN logs, admin portal authentication logs, Active Directory logs, email logs (phishing suspects), endpoint detection alerts, and firewall logs for the past 72 hours. The CEO wants a full investigation by end of day. Investigate this incident to determine: (1) how the attacker gained access to the admin portal (phishing, credential stuffing, session hijacking, or insider), (2) the complete attack timeline from initial compromise to fund transfer execution, (3) which user accounts were compromised and how, (4) whether this is an external attacker or insider threat, (5) the full scope of data accessed beyond the wire transfers, (6) IOCs (IPs, domains, file hashes, email addresses) for threat intelligence sharing, and (7) immediate containment and evidence preservation steps. Provide a complete incident investigation report suitable for executive briefing and law enforcement handoff.
evals.expected_output: A comprehensive incident investigation report containing: (1) Executive summary suitable for CEO/board briefing with incident classification (external APT, phishing-based BEC, insider threat, or credential compromise), total financial impact, and current containment status, (2) Detailed minute-by-minute timeline from initial compromise (phishing email click, VPN login, or first suspicious action) through lateral movement, privilege escalation, and wire transfer execution, with all timestamps in UTC and evidence source for each event, (3) Root cause analysis identifying the initial access vector with specific evidence (e.g., phishing email with malicious attachment at XX:XX UTC, credential stuffing from IP X.X.X.X, or session token theft), (4) Complete list of compromised accounts with how each was accessed and what actions were performed under each, (5) Attacker identification section with all IOCs: source IPs with geolocation and reputation, domains and URLs, email addresses and subjects, file hashes of any malware, and MITRE ATT&CK technique mapping, (6) Clear assessment of external vs insider threat with supporting reasoning, (7) Impact quantification covering: financial loss ($2.3M in wires), data accessed (customer PII, account numbers), systems compromised, and regulatory notification requirements, (8) Evidence preservation summary with chain of custody documentation for all collected artifacts, (9) Immediate containment recommendations (account lockouts, IP blocks, credential resets, system isolation), (10) Short and long-term remediation recommendations, and (11) Law enforcement handoff package summary with all IOCs and evidence packaged for FBI/Secret Service referral.
